samples.summary: stampLens' defensive branches (non-array input, non-string lensId, null/malformed members) are untested
samples.evidence: `stampLens` (review-panel.mjs:812-817) has three coercion branches: `Array.isArray(findings) ? findings : []`, `typeof lensId === "string" ? lensId : ""`, and the `f && typeof f === "object"` guard that passes junk through. None of the five new tests exercises any of them — all calls pass a real array and the string LENS_ID (test file 3232, 3263, 3278, 3297). The `lensId` fallback is the notable one: stamping `lens: ""` makes `findingSimilarity` (rounds.mjs:303) treat the finding as same-lens as any rebuttal whose `lens` is also blank, so the untested branch is exactly the one that could produce a wrong rebuttal match. Searched review-panel.test.mjs for every `stampLens` call site and found no negative/edge-case case.

samples.summary: The "stamping preserves object IDENTITY" test does not actually test stampLens' identity preservation; it tests gatingFindings
samples.evidence: The test builds `merged = stampLens(clusterFindings(dedupeFindings([freshFinding()])), LENS_ID)` — the input finding has no `lens`, so stampLens returns a COPY (`{ ...f, lens: id }`). The assertions (`gating[0] === merged[0]` and the `merged.filter(...)` removal) therefore only prove that `gatingFindings` filters without copying and that `adjudicateRebuttals` returns the original objects; they would pass unchanged even if stampLens copied unconditionally. The genuine no-copy guarantee is only covered by the separate already-stamped test (3290-3299), which does not go through the merge/gate/adjudicate chain the comment says depends on it. The test is not vacuous (the end-to-end removal is real), but its stated claim is not what it verifies.

samples.summary: The wiring test asserts source text, so it cannot catch a runtime mis-wiring (wrong lens value, stamping applied after a copy)
samples.evidence: `test("the round loop actually routes `merged` through stampLens")` reads review-panel.mjs as a string and regex-matches the single `const merged =` line. `assert.match(assignments[0], /lens\.id/)` matches `lens.id` anywhere on the line, not in stampLens' second argument, so a line like `stampLens(clusterFindings(dedupeFindings([...priorForLens.filter(p => p.lens === lens.id)])), other.id)` would still pass. The test also cannot observe the actual per-lens loop in `main()` (review-panel.mjs:2480-2506), so the mergedAfter identity chain in production remains untested at runtime — the test acknowledges this itself. Acceptable as a stopgap, but the coverage it advertises is textual only.

samples.summary: No test covers the downstream effect of newly-stamped `lens` on the summary / stage-detail / cross-round comparison paths
samples.evidence: Fresh findings previously reached `buildStageDetail`, the check-run body and the persisted round state with no `lens` property; after this change every finding in `merged` carries one (review-panel.mjs:2480, flowing into `mergedAfter` at 2506 and `writeStageDetail(... buildStageDetail(...))` at 2525). `findingSimilarity` gates on lens equality (rounds.mjs:303) and is also used by `repeatRatio`/`detectStalledRounds` and `finding-match.mjs`, so the extra field can change matching outcomes for consumers of the persisted findings. The five new tests only cover stampLens itself plus the rebuttal match; none asserts that serialisation, gating output, or cross-round matching is unchanged. Searched review-panel.test.mjs for buildStageDetail/stage-detail tests near the new block and for any test combining stampLens with buildStageDetail — none exists.
searchedFor: grep buildStageDetail in review-panel.test.mjs (diff context line 3209)

samples.summary: The merged-cluster case (fresh + prior collapsing into a rewritten representative) is only tested for byte-identical summaries, i.e. the dedupe path, not the clusterFindings path stampLens is placed after
samples.evidence: In the first new test `fresh` and `prior` share the same file and summary, so `dedupeFindings` (review-panel.mjs:553-568) collapses them by key and `clusterFindings` never runs `mergeCluster` with two members. The motivating scenario in the comment — a fresh REWORDING merging with its carried-forward twin, where `mergeCluster` returns a fresh `{ ...rep }` copy (review-panel.mjs:655-664) and the FRESH representative wins — is therefore never exercised. A test using different-but-similar summaries would cover the actual path the fix exists for. Searched the new test block (3209-3319) for any pair of differing summaries; both fixtures use the same DEFECT constant.
